title: Felicis hires Graham Littlehale to lead hard-tech startup focus
excerpt: The venture capital firm, best known for bets on Shopify, Notion, and Mercor, has hired a new partner to invest in physical world technologies.
content_html:
Exclusive

The VC firm behind Shopify is doubling down on robotics and defense

By Rya Jetha

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Hard tech used to be a hard sell in Silicon Valley. Now, a major venture firm is staffing up to invest in it.

Felicis, the Bay Area venture capital firm best known for bets on Shopify, Notion, and Mercor, has hired Graham Littlehale as a partner to invest in aerospace, defense, energy, manufacturing, and robotics, the firm told Business Insider.

Littlehale joins from Point72 Ventures, where he was an early member of its national security investing team. His investments there included Stoke Space, which is developing reusable rockets, and Rune Technologies, which builds software for military logistics.

The hire signals that Felicis is doubling down on companies building for the physical world. The firm has already backed CoreWeave, which provides AI companies with access to advanced chips; Crusoe, which develops AI data centers; and Skild AI, which is building a general-purpose "brain" for robots.

"The physical world is entering its own software moment," said Aydin Senkut, an early Google employee who founded Felicis two decades ago. "Graham has spent his career backing founders at the forefront of hard tech transformations, making him a natural fit to help deepen Felicis's commitment to the founders redefining the physical economy."

Across the valley, investors are paying renewed attention to hardware as AI moves from chatbots into machines, costs fall, labor shortages grow, and geopolitical pressures push companies to reshore supply chains.

Robotics and physical AI startups, which build machines that operate in the real world, raised $16.3 billion across 492 deals in the first quarter of 2026. It was the strongest quarter on record for both capital invested and deal count, according to PitchBook.

Littlehale has been making bets on physical technology long before it became fashionable. He began his career a decade ago, investing in natural resources and energy infrastructure.

"When I was 22 and investing in energy, and my friends were investing in SaaS, I was like, 'I get to go see an oil rig, and I think that's way more cool,'" Littlehale said. After working on commercial expansion at self-driving startup Nuro from 2021 to 2022, Littlehale realized he missed investing and joined Point72 the following year.

At Felicis, Littlehale plans to focus on "manufacturing foundation models," or AI systems that could take a product from concept through production. He is also interested in digital tools that accelerate hardware development and robots designed for industries, including construction.

Littlehale thinks robotics foundation models may follow the reverse trajectory of large language models. Chatbots started with broad, general-purpose models that were later specialized. Robots, he said, may have to begin by mastering individual tasks, then combine those skills into more general intelligence.

"The idea is, 'Let's fold a bunch of laundry and make a bunch of coffees, and then we will have enough things that are close to each other that we can generalize,'" he said.

Littlehale will also pursue investments in space and undersea technology, two areas he considers critical to US economic resilience and national security. Both sectors have become crowded and, at times, overhyped, he said, though opportunities remain for investors willing to take a longer view.

He pointed to his recent investment in Endurance Energy, a startup developing technology to generate geothermal energy from heat beneath the ocean floor.

"That is not something you can invest in based on a hype cycle," Littlehale said. "It is a decadeslong bet."

此次聘用表明 Felicis 正在加倍致力于为实体世界打造公司。 该公司已经支持了 CoreWeave，该公司为人工智能公司提供了先进芯片的使用途径； Crusoe，开发人工智能数据中心； Skild AI 正在为机器人构建通用“大脑”。

“物理世界正在进入自己的软件时代，”二十年前创立 Felicis 的谷歌早期员工艾丁·森库特 (Aydin Senkut) 说道。 “格雷厄姆的职业生涯一直在支持处于硬技术转型最前沿的创始人，这使他成为帮助加深 Felicis 对创始人重新定义实体经济的承诺的天然人选。”

随着人工智能从聊天机器人转向机器、成本下降、劳动力短缺加剧以及地缘政治压力迫使企业重新部署供应链，硅谷各地的投资者重新开始关注硬件。

制造在现实世界中运行的机器的机器人和物理人工智能初创公司在 2026 年第一季度通过 492 笔交易筹集了 163 亿美元。 根据 PitchBook 的数据，无论是资本投资还是交易数量，本季度都是有记录以来最强劲的季度。

早在物理技术成为时尚之前，Littlehale 就一直在押注它。 他十年前开始了自己的职业生涯，投资自然资源和能源基础设施。

“当我 22 岁时投资能源，我的朋友们投资 SaaS 时，我当时想，‘我可以去看石油钻井平台，我认为这更酷，’”Littlehale 说。 2021 年至 2022 年，Littlehale 在自动驾驶初创公司 Nuro 从事商业扩张工作后，意识到自己错过了投资机会，并于次年加入了 Point72。

在 Felicis，Littlehale 计划专注于“制造基础模型”，即可以将产品从概念到生产的人工智能系统。 他还对加速硬件开发的数字工具以及为建筑等行业设计的机器人感兴趣。

Littlehale 认为机器人基础模型可能会遵循大型语言模型的相反轨迹。 聊天机器人最初采用广泛的通用模型，后来又进行了专门化。 他说，机器人可能必须从掌握单独的任务开始，然后将这些技能结合成更通用的智能。

“我们的想法是，‘让我们叠一堆衣服，煮一堆咖啡，然后我们就会有足够多的彼此接近的东西，我们可以进行概括，’”他说。

利特尔黑尔还将寻求对太空和海底技术的投资，他认为这两个领域对美国经济弹性和国家安全至关重要。 他表示，这两个行业都已变得拥挤不堪，有时甚至被过度炒作，但愿意放长远眼光的投资者仍然有机会。

他提到了他最近对 Endurance Energy 的投资，这是一家开发利用海底热量产生地热能技术的初创公司。

“这不是你可以根据炒作周期进行投资的东西，”利特尔黑尔说。 “这是一个长达数十年的赌注。”
